searchText: Totally random exploration question: would we have been better off if the EVM was a higher level language? Say, make the EVM something similar to LLL Right now, compilers feel complex in a lot of ways, and a lot of that is because the EVM is "close to the metal". But in reality there's no good reason for the EVM to be close to the metal eg. right now we have *two* ways to make calls: calls that get compiled into jumps, and calls that are calls A from-scratch higher-level EVM might not have bytes memory, but it would have a built-in concept of variables, calls, conditionals, loops... There's a risk it'd have been a less versatile compiler target, would have over-determined the nature of (yet higher level) languages which might plausibly target it. What kind of languages might have been deterred by this kind of EVM? I feel like Move-like langs would be about as easy as today, maybe even easier I guess "existing langs" (eg. Rust) compiling to EVM would be harder Although.... WASM is a higher-level VM, and lots of langs compile to WASM just fine!
